subject: `\@a[0,1]` does not distribute the ref over the slice — one ref instead of one per element
description:
Found s361 while writing the inverse guards for the foreach-single-scalar fix (scratchpad fe3.pl, row M3). Pre-existing — reproduces at the session-start commit 197dcd9, so it is NOT from that fix.

  my @a = ('a','b','c');
  my $n = 0;
  $n++ for (\@a[0,1]);      # perl: 2 iterations (a ref PER ELEMENT)
  print $n;                 # PCL:  1

perl's `\` distributes over a slice (and over a parenthesised list, `\(@a)`), yielding one reference per element; PCL builds a single reference to the slice. `\(@a)` itself is CORRECT in PCL (3 = one ref per element, verified s361), so the distribution machinery exists — it is the SLICE operand that misses it.

Low priority (niche), but it is a silent-wrong: the count and the values are both wrong with no diagnostic. The foreach fix's predicate `Pl::Parser::_foreach_single_scalar_p` deliberately DECLINES `\`-cast-plus-postfix for exactly this reason, so the two do not interact — fixing this one does not need the predicate changed.</description>
</invoke>
